newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: TENNIS-SAMPRAS WINS SWISS INDOOR FOR YEAR'S SEVENTH TITLE.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-SAMPRAS WINS SWISS INDOOR FOR YEAR'S SEVENTH TITLE.

text.p: World number one Pete Sampras breezed to his seventh tournament win of the season with a straight sets victory over Hendrik Dreekmann at the Swiss indoor championship on Sunday.
The 7-5 6-2 6-0 win gave the 25-year-old American his 43rd career title and kept his 100 percent record intact, having won all seven finals he has appeared in this year.
The match unravelled quickly for the 21-year-old German after Sampras broke him at 6-5 to take the first set.
Sampras then opened the second with another break, bolting to 3-0 lead to take control of the set and match.
It was the same scenario in the third as Sampras simply overwhelmed Dreekmann, shutting out the nervous German to wrap up the match in one hour 22 minutes.
"I didn't have a chance," said Dreekmann. "He was serving so well and if you can't return his serve you can't break him."
Sampras collected $137,000 in his first appearance since he won the U.S. Open earlier this month. His prize money for the the season rose to more than $1.7 million.
Sampras blasted 19 aces past the stunned Dreekmann. "I played well today, I served big," said the American.
"After the first set I saw him hang his head and I realised it was going to be a tough battle for him to come back.
"I actually surprised myself here. I thought I would have a letdown after the U.S. Open but I didn't."
It was the third consecutive tournament success for Sampras, who said he would return home on Monday and prepare for Stuttgart, Paris and the ATP Tour championship in Hanover.
"Those will be big tournaments," said Sampras, the first world number one to play at the Swiss indoors since Bjorn Borg in 1980.
"My goal is to finish the year number one again and winning here was a good start."
